About the Occupational Therapy event

Occupational Therapy is a Health Professions event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons following the HOSA Occupational Therapy 2026–27 test plan and all eight Round Two instruction skills, built from the official references (O’Brien and Conners, Atchison and Dirette, and the OT Toolkit for skills). Includes models of practice, activity analysis, adaptive dressing and floor-transfer drills, heart-rate monitoring, body mechanics, posture and stretch-break sequences, plus cases across the lifespan. Always follow the scenario and rating sheets you are given.

Occupational Therapy practice tests

Each test is an original, full-length simulation of the HOSA Round One written test, written to run slightly harder than the real thing. Every answer comes with an explanation and a reference.

  • Practice Test 1Full-length Round One simulation50 questions · 60 min
  • Practice Test 2Full-length Round One simulation50 questions · 60 min

Sample Occupational Therapy questions

1. A stroke survivor’s weak shoulder hangs and partly slips out of the joint. Which approach helps protect it?

  1. Pulling on the arm during transfers
  2. Supporting the arm on a lapboard
  3. Letting the arm hang freely
  4. Lifting the patient by the arm
Show answer

B. Supporting the arm on a lapboard

Shoulder subluxation is common after stroke. Supporting the arm and avoiding pulling on it reduce pain and further injury.

2. Which tool often helps children with autism manage transitions during the school day?

  1. Unexpected changes in routine
  2. Long verbal instructions
  3. Louder classrooms
  4. A visual schedule
Show answer

D. A visual schedule

Visual schedules make the day predictable and reduce anxiety about transitions.

3. What does trauma-informed care emphasize?

  1. Requiring clients to describe their trauma
  2. Using physical restraint first
  3. Making all decisions for the client
  4. Safety, trust and client choice
Show answer

D. Safety, trust and client choice

Trauma-informed care recognizes the effects of trauma and avoids retraumatizing clients by emphasizing safety, collaboration and empowerment.
